title: Mexico Has Built 4,000 Kilometers of Roads by Hand Since 2018, National Indigenous Peoples Institute Says
author: Alonso Urrutia and Alma E. Muñoz
content:
_This article by[Alonso Urrutia and Alma E.
Muñoz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alonso%20Urrutia%20y%20Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz)
originally appeared in the [November 19, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/19/politica/se-han-
construido-4-mil-kilometros-de-caminos-artesanales-desde-2018-inpi), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** Since the [Hand-Built
Roads](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/11/estados/supervisan-
construccion-de-caminos-artesanales-en-la-montana-alta-y-baja-de-guerrero)
program was established in Indigenous communities in December 2018, 578 roads
have been built, with a combined length of **4,000 kilometers in 17 states** ,
equivalent to the distance between Los Angeles, California, and Tapachula,
Chiapas, reported Adelfo Regino, head of the National Institute of Indigenous
Peoples. He also said the institute is working on twenty justice plans for
Indigenous peoples.

For his part, Infrastructure, Communications and Transportation Secretary
Jesús Esteva said projections for the current six-year presidential term call
for the construction of **4,550 kilometers** with an investment of **32
billion pesos** in 18 states. He explained that in 2025, 135 hand-built roads
were constructed, totaling 368 kilometers, with an investment of 2.6 billion
pesos, while in 2026 the goal is to complete 389 roads totaling 900
kilometers, with an investment of 6 billion pesos.

Regino recalled that the program began in December 2018, at the start of
President Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s administration, in the community of
Analco, in Oaxaca’s northern mountains. It gradually expanded to the rest of
Oaxaca, then to Guerrero and the Purépecha Plateau, and now reaches 18 states.
